acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

header.tag_why: The COO, who signed with Adyen, judged the deal on store returns at the till, installs and rollout credibility, and we answered with a partner and a description where Adyen brought a retail team and references she knew.

evidence.excerpt: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: they'd just launched a loyalty program that was supposed to work everywhere and didn't, because store and web were two different customer records.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Their COO, Angela, apparently stood in a store on December 27th watching the returns queue.
evidence.label: opinion

trigger.insight: The pain started at the returns counter and in a split customer record. It belonged to the COO and store operations, not to checkout conversion. We ran it as a web RFP through the CTO while the origin story everyone at the customer told was about a store returns queue.
trigger.messaging: Open store-heavy deals with the cross-channel return and the single customer record, not with M1's global-currency opener or the web checkout.

evidence.excerpt: The CTO, Raj. He ran the RFP, he was my contact the whole way.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Angela.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: ...Probably Angela. Raj wanted us. I think.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Once. The kickoff.
evidence.label: fact

decider.insight: Tom named Raj with confidence and then reversed when he was asked who signed. Angela signed, her team asked for the store workshop, and Tom met her once. Our whole read of the deal (ahead, Raj wants us) came from someone who did not make the call. How much weight Raj's preference actually carried is unclear.
decider.messaging: Write store messaging for the COO and head of store operations as the economic buyers, with an operations-led narrative alongside the technical RFP.

evidence.excerpt: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: they named retailers Angela knew
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Before, it was all web. Conversion, checkout, wallets. After, it was stores.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Raj forwarded me a list of 14 questions and 11 of them were about stores.
evidence.label: fact

competitor.insight: By Raj's secondhand account (Tom wasn't there), Adyen did not try to beat us on web. They moved the evaluation onto stores, using people with rollout experience and peers the COO recognised. The 11-of-14 question list shows the reframing worked before we noticed it.
competitor.messaging: Counter rollout-credibility pitches with named store-rollout people and retail references the buyer can call, not slides about platform unity.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the online checkout demo. Their ecommerce lead loved it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Silence: the unified commerce part.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: 'that's a diagram.'
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev

evidence.excerpt: Then she asked how a return works. Step by step. At the till.
evidence.label: fact

message.insight: M3 was read out word for word and the head of store operations dismissed it as a diagram. The applause came from the ecommerce lead, who did not decide. Our strongest material landed with the side of the business that lost the vote.
message.messaging: Replace M3's abstract claim with a step-by-step, at-the-till walkthrough of an online order being returned in store.

evidence.excerpt: When Bev asked who does the installs, I said we'd bring in a partner. She wrote something down and didn't ask another question.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: They had six people from store operations.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Right before that, honestly, we were ahead. Raj said so. We'd won the web side.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Angela's team. Stores.
evidence.label: fact

decided.insight: The loss crystallised when Tom said a partner would do the installs, which is exactly the 'two vendors pointing at each other' the COO said she didn't want. Being 'ahead' only meant winning the web side with the CTO. Tom's closing view that 'we had the better product online' repeats the same blind spot.
decided.messaging: State plainly who owns installs and store rollout end to end, and if a partner is involved, frame us as the single accountable party.

evidence.excerpt: 'can I talk to them?'
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: we couldn't set up a call in time.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Then a rollout plan. Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We described it. We never showed it.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: Three asks went unmet: a reference call, a dated rollout plan, and a live cross-channel return. We answered each with a document or a description. The transcript doesn't establish whether we could have done the live return, only that we never showed it. M8's 'see our customer stories' is the wrong format for a buyer who wants a phone call.
gaps.messaging: Back store claims with a callable retail reference and a live till-return demo, not case studies.

evidence.excerpt: 'One system for the tills and the website.'
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev

evidence.excerpt: 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.'
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: 'one customer, one basket.'
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: We kept saying 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale.' They said 'the tills.'
evidence.label: fact

language.insight: The customer talked about tills, one basket and accountability. We talked about unified commerce, point of sale and in-person payments. Angela's line about two vendors shows that her real worry was single ownership when something breaks, and our partner-install answer made that worry worse.
language.messaging: Use their words, 'one system for the tills and the website' and 'one customer, one basket', and add an explicit one-throat-to-choke accountability line.

gaps.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Raj (via Tom) whether Angela overruled his recommendation or he recommended Adyen in the end, and what tipped it.

gaps.question: What did Bev write down after the partner-install answer, and what did the store team conclude from the workshop?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Raj or Bev for the workshop takeaways or scoring the store team shared internally.

gaps.question: Why couldn't we set up a reference call in time, and could we have demoed a live online-to-store return?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom and the solutions engineer what blocked the reference and the live return demo.

close.rep_takeaway: When the trigger story lives in the stores and the COO, the deal lives there too. Get to that person beyond the kickoff, and when they ask to see, call or plan something, show it live, connect them, or put dates on it, because describing it is how we lost this one.
